clue.text: The ruination of parties a hanger-on can be

indicators.note: ruining the word parties and the a after it wrecks their order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who sponges off others can ruin any party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The ruination of' tells you to rearrange PARTIES plus A; 'can be' is only a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasite is a sponger who lives off others, which is what a hanger-on does.

clue.text: Tips, though no tip's necessary

indicators.note: what is necessary must be worked out of no tip's, so its letters are rearranged into a new word

parts.note: the letters N, O, T, I, P and S, the 's counting as a letter here

explanation.surface: A remark that you needn't leave a gratuity, though tips are mentioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'necessary' is a loose signal to rearrange NO TIPS; the apostrophe S counts here because it stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharp ends are points, so tips and points are synonyms.

clue.text: Some malefactor — a scallywag — a scoundrel

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A list of words for a villain: malefactor, scallywag, scoundrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A rascal is a rogue or knave, the same thing as a scoundrel.

clue.text: Changed course, and could well be beaten

explanation.definitionFit: Switched means swapped direction or track; it also means whipped with a switch, a thin cane, so a beaten person was switched.

clue.text: A word of advice about the right excursion

indicators.note: the word of advice goes about, that is around, the letter for right

parts.note: a tip is a helpful hint
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone offering advice on the best outing to take.
explanation.definitionFit: A trip is a short journey or outing, the same as an excursion.

clue.text: Hammered when a couple of thousand in the red

indicators.note: the two thousands sit in, that is inside, the word for the red colour

parts.note: taken as the colour word red
taken as written
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so a couple of them give MM

explanation.surface: A business taking a beating after running up a two-thousand debt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the red' reads as being in debt, but 'in' is the container signal and 'the red' is only the colour; 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Rammed means struck or driven hard, as a hammer drives a nail.

clue.text: A base with an oil-refining place

parts.note: taken as written
base in the sense of low or wicked is bad
taken as written

explanation.surface: A military base paired with an oil refinery.
explanation.walkthrough: ABADAN is a port city in south-west Iran, famous for its large oil refinery.
explanation.definitionFit: Abadan is an Iranian city whose huge refinery made it a centre of the oil industry.

clue.text: Males score in intellect!

parts.note: men are males
a score is a count or tally

explanation.surface: A jibe that men keep score on brains.
explanation.definitionFit: Mentally means with regard to the mind, that is, in the matter of thinking power.

clue.text: Manage people's presentation

parts.note: to do is to manage, as in 'we'll do somehow'
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: Advice on running a country's public relations.
explanation.definitionFit: A donation is a gift, something presented, so a presentation in that sense.

clue.text: Encourage the serving of the currently popular drink

parts.note: something fashionable right now is in
spirit is strong alcoholic drink such as whisky or gin

explanation.surface: Serving the fashionable cocktail of the moment to lift the mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the serving of the' is padding that joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspirit is to fill with courage or enliven, a synonym of hearten.

clue.text: Against toting a woman's gun

indicators.note: toting means carrying, so the word for against carries the woman inside it

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
Ann is a woman's name

explanation.surface: Someone opposed to a woman carrying a firearm.
explanation.definitionFit: A cannon is a large artillery piece, a big gun.

clue.text: Repairing a road in quiet times is an absurdity

indicators.note: the rearranged road letters sit in, between, the letters for quiet and times

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for soft
X is the multiplication sign

indicators.note: repairing the words a road means putting their letters back together in a new order

explanation.surface: Fixing a road during quiet periods turns out to be absurd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repairing' makes ARADO from A ROAD, which goes in P and X.
explanation.definitionFit: A paradox is a self-contradictory statement, something that seems an absurdity.

clue.text: Roofing of the church specified

parts.note: that points to a specified thing, as in 'that one'

explanation.surface: Asking what roofing material the church specified.
explanation.definitionFit: Thatch is straw or reeds laid as a covering on top of a building.

clue.text: A real downpour may impair the vision

explanation.definitionFit: A cataract is a torrent or deluge of water; it is also a clouding of the eye's lens that dims sight.

clue.text: A number leave no doubt about blame

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
to ensure something is to make certain of it

explanation.surface: Several people make sure who's at fault.
explanation.definitionFit: To censure is to criticise or condemn, which is to blame.

clue.text: Enlarge accommodation for top brass

indicators.note: accommodation here is adjustment, so the letters of enlarge are adjusted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Expanding the quarters provided for senior officers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accommodation' means adjustment here, the signal to rearrange ENLARGE, and is not lodging.
explanation.definitionFit: A general is a senior army officer, one of the top brass.

clue.text: Muse about regal animal losing tail

parts.note: C is circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: losing its tail means the last letter of the animal word is dropped

parts.note: the lion is called the king of beasts

explanation.surface: A poet musing on a big cat that has lost its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Muse' looks like a verb; it is one of the nine Muses of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Clio is one of the nine Greek Muses, the one who presides over history.

clue.text: The eccentric hands out quite a lot

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters of hands out are put in an odd order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An oddball distributing gifts generously.
explanation.definitionFit: A thousand is a large number, so it is a fair amount, quite a lot.

clue.text: Cold, over-tired — in a sorry state indeed

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on taps
on means over, as in a lid on top of a jar
tired in the sense of stale or hackneyed is trite

explanation.surface: Chilly and exhausted, someone is in a miserable condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over-tired' reads as one word; split it into 'over' and 'tired'. 'indeed' just closes the sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Contrite means remorseful, feeling sorry for a wrong done.

clue.text: Retiring military men did what military men do

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
soldiers serve, so to do as they do is to have served

explanation.surface: Soldiers retiring after they did their duty.
explanation.definitionFit: Retiring and reserved both describe a shy, reticent person.

clue.text: Capital cover for a poet!

explanation.definitionFit: A hood covers the head, and capital can mean head; Thomas Hood was a 19th-century English poet.

clue.text: A pushy individual in the Midlands

parts.note: taken as written
someone who shoves is a shover

explanation.surface: Describing a pushy person living in central England.
explanation.walkthrough: ASHOVER is a village in Derbyshire, in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashover is a village in Derbyshire, a county of the East Midlands region.

clue.text: A trick to hold the ring and so cause excitement

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the trick word holds the ring letter within it

parts.note: a ruse is a trick
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A magician's trick with a ring that thrills the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: To arouse is to stir up or excite, which is to cause excitement.

clue.text: Sound procedure needing refinement

parts.note: a course of action is a procedure

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like praise of the procedure but signals that COURSE, said aloud, gives COARSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse means rough or crude, so lacking polish and needing refinement.

clue.text: Cattle drives

explanation.definitionFit: Steers are young castrated bulls, and to steer a vehicle is to drive it.

clue.text: They circulate — so they say

clue.text: Reformed rotter's comeback

explanation.definitionFit: A retort is a sharp reply, a comeback in an argument.

clue.text: The staff of an American writer about fifty

indicators.note: the writer goes about, around, the Roman numeral for fifty

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe was an American writer
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: The staff of a US author who is around fifty years old.

clue.text: Hostility is total in a recession

parts.note: a sum is a total
taken as written
taken as written

clue.text: Clubs on the border tend to get together

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for the card suit clubs
taken as written
a verge is an edge or border, as a grass verge beside a road

explanation.surface: Golfers on the edge of the green tend to gather.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines that converge move towards one point, coming closer and meeting.

clue.text: The weight-watcher must be put off grabbing one

indicators.note: the word for put off grabs the letter for one and holds it inside

parts.note: to deter is to discourage or put off

clue.text: Irritates the school head, and that's quite uncalled for

indicators.note: head means the first letter of the word school

explanation.walkthrough: 'school head' suggests a headteacher; it means the first letter of 'school'.
